There are two small rivers, A and B, near it; River A is on the left side of the figure, and River B is on the right side. Water diversion lines 1 and 3 are located in the northwest-west direction of the small town and are relatively far from the small town; lines 2 and 4 are located on the east-southeast side of the small town and close to River B, among which line 4 is closer to the river section on the southeast side of the small town and has a shorter route. Judging from the positions of the contour lines, the river section near the southeast side of River B is relatively favorable for diverting water from a higher place to the small town; lines 1 and 3 are relatively long and cross more undulating terrain, so they are unreasonable; although line 2 is close to River B, compared with line 4, it is not as favorable as diverting water from the nearby river section on the southeast side for self-flow and the route is not as simple. Line 4 is introduced from the nearer River B section on the southeast side of the small town, with a short route and better terrain conditions, facilitating gravity water conveyance, so it is the most reasonable.

Read the graphic materials and answer in combination with relevant knowledge: Which water diversion line entering the small town in the figure is the most reasonable? Please fill in the serial number. <image1>
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the small town is located in the lower-middle part of the map frame. There are two small rivers, A and B, near it; River A is on the left side of the figure, and River B is on the right side. The figure has contour lines and river lines, and marks 4 dashed water diversion lines leading toward the vicinity of the small town, numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4 respectively. Water diversion lines 1 and 3 are located in the northwest-west direction of the small town and are relatively far from the small town; lines 2 and 4 are located on the east-southeast side of the small town and close to River B, among which line 4 is closer to the river section on the southeast side of the small town and has a shorter route.
Reasoning: The question stem states that the flow volumes of the two small rivers are equivalent, so there is no need to compare the water volumes of Rivers A and B. When choosing a water diversion line in a hilly area, priority should be given to taking water from a higher place to facilitate self-flow water conveyance; at the same time, the route should be as short as possible and should reduce crossing complex undulating terrain. Judging from the positions of the contour lines, the river section near the southeast side of River B is relatively favorable for diverting water from a higher place to the small town; lines 1 and 3 are relatively long and cross more undulating terrain, so they are unreasonable; although line 2 is close to River B, compared with line 4, it is not as favorable as diverting water from the nearby river section on the southeast side for self-flow and the route is not as simple. Line 4 is introduced from the nearer River B section on the southeast side of the small town, with a short route and better terrain conditions, facilitating gravity water conveyance, so it is the most reasonable.
